S01: The Cyclopes were sons of Poseidon.
S02: The god was enraged by what had befallen Polyphemus.
S03: He raised yet another storm, aimed at the ships of Odysseus.
S04: But this time the ships found refuge.
S05: In the land of Aeolus, the god of the wind.
S07: Odysseus: "Ten years of war... and Ithaca still awaits me home."
S08: Aeolus: "Take this bag. Within it are all the winds."
S09: The winds could have stopped him from reaching Ithaca.
S10: The ships set sail again, with wind at their backs.
S11: Soon, on the horizon, appeared the island of Ithaca.
S12: Two crews gazed toward home — but curiosity was already waking.
S13: Some of the sailors coveted the mysterious bag.
S14: With one tug, the knot came undone.
S15: Out of it came a tornado.
S16: It swept the ships back out to the open sea.
S17: Then, a shore rose before them.
S18: They were forced to anchor at the island of Circe.
S19: And there another misfortune awaited them.
S20: Out of the darkness came the sorceress Circe.
S21: Circe: "I shall turn you into swine."
S22: With a wave of her wand, the light covered them.
S23: One by one, the men began to change.
S24: The hall filled with swine in place of brave sailors.
S25: Odysseus: "What have you done to them? Give me back my men!"
S27: Odysseus walked out of the hall with a heavy heart.
S29: In his hand he held an herb with bright flowers.
S30: Hermes: "Crush it into boiling water. It will protect you from her curse."
S31: Odysseus made a potion of the herbs.
S32: With one sip, his body became resistant.
S33: He returned before the sorceress, stronger than her magic.
S34: Circe raised her wand — but the beam shattered.
S36: Odysseus: "Restore their human form — or you will face a sword, not words."
S37: Circe raised her hands, and the light softened.
S38: One by one, the swine began to rise.
S39: Their faces returned, brighter than before.
S40: Odysseus's men stood on their feet again.
S41: Odysseus: "Now return us home, and we will go in peace."
S42: The ships were repaired, and the wind — merciful.
S43: Odysseus stood at the prow's end and gazed toward the horizon.
S44: His heart was calm: Ithaca was no longer far.
S45: With a full crew, the ships sailed out into the night.
S46: Behind them, the island of Circe slowly melted into mist.
S47: Before them stretched the sea — the road home.
S48: On the horizon, Ithaca awaited them.
